title: fix(polli-cli): warn when text generation hits its token limit
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16234

`polli gen text` currently treats explicit token-limit termination like normal completion, including empty answers. This adds a nonfatal stderr warning while preserving useful output.

- Warn once for the first completion's `finish_reason: length`, in buffered, file and streaming modes.
- Retain a streamed length indication through trailing choice-less usage/null metadata; SSE parser changes expose types only.
- Preserve stdout/JSON shape, file bytes, metadata and exit status. Do not infer truncation from empty content or change API limits/retries.
- Extend existing command tests for empty/partial output and non-length controls.

Validation: 12 regressions fail on baseline; all 30 focused tests and 275 wider CLI tests pass. CLI ESM/declaration build, Biome and seven offline built-CLI controls pass. Local tests used cached Vitest 2.1.9; three loopback-server suites were excluded under the existing sandbox restriction. Strict scoped TypeScript reports the same pre-existing `src/lib/api.ts:23` TS2322 on baseline and fix.

gist.headline: The bee flags the cutoff
gist.blurb: When `polli gen text` runs out of tokens, it gives a quiet heads-up on stderr instead of treating the cutoff like a tidy ending. The useful bits still go where you asked them to.
gist.summary: `polli gen text` adds one nonfatal stderr warning when the first completion ends with `finish_reason: length`, across buffered, file, and streaming modes, while preserving stdout, JSON shape, file bytes, metadata, and exit status.
gist.impact: CLI users can tell when a response hit its token limit—even if the answer is empty—without changes to their output files, pipelines, or API limits.
gist.visual_concept: Polli inspects a retro terminal where a growing line of text stops at a small token-limit marker; a gentle warning appears on a separate stderr display while the saved output remains untouched. A little code-plant beside the terminal keeps the scene warm and grounded.
